content: Esomeprazole is a medication prescribed to treat gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD), a condition where stomach acid flows backward into the esophagus, causing heartburn and potential damage to the esophagus. It is used to alleviate GERD symptoms, promote healing of the esophagus, and prevent further damage. Additionally, it is sometimes used in combination with other medications to prevent stomach ulcers. Esomeprazole belongs to a class of drugs known as proton pump inhibitors, which work by reducing the amount of acid produced in the stomach. Esomeprazole is available as a delayed-release capsule taken orally, typically once daily, at least one hour before a meal. To ensure consistent use, it is recommended to take it at the same time each day. Follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully, and consult your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Take the medication exactly as directed, without altering the dose or frequency. Swallow the capsules whole; do not split, chew, or crush them. If swallowing the capsule is difficult, you can open it and sprinkle the pellets onto one tablespoon of cool, soft applesauce. Mix the pellets with the applesauce and swallow the mixture immediately without chewing. Do not save the mixture for later use. Your doctor will determine the duration of your treatment. For GERD, treatment may last 4–8 weeks or longer. For ulcers, esomeprazole may be taken with other medications for 10 days. Your doctor will also advise you on when you can expect to experience the full benefits of the medication. If your symptoms worsen or do not improve, contact your doctor. Continue taking esomeprazole even if you feel well, and do not stop without consulting your doctor. Esomeprazole may also be prescribed for other uses. Consult your doctor or pharmacist for additional information. Before taking esomeprazole, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to esomeprazole, other proton pump inhibitors (e.g., lansoprazole, omeprazole, pantoprazole, rabeprazole), or any other medications. Provide a complete list of all prescription and nonprescription medications, vitamins, supplements, and herbal products you are taking, especially anticoagulants (e.g., warfarin), digoxin, iron supplements, or ketoconazole. Your doctor may need to adjust your medication doses or monitor you for side effects. If you are taking digoxin, iron supplements, or ketoconazole, take these at least two hours before esomeprazole. Inform your doctor if you have a history of liver disease, are pregnant, plan to become pregnant, or are breastfeeding. If you become pregnant while taking esomeprazole, notify your doctor. You may take antacids with esomeprazole, but consult your doctor for recommendations on which antacid to use and how to take it. Discuss your diet with your doctor, as certain foods and drinks may worsen your symptoms. Your doctor can advise you on which items to avoid or consume in moderation. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue your regular schedule. Do not take a double dose to compensate for a missed one. Esomeprazole may cause side effects. Common minor side effects include headache, diarrhea, upset stomach, gas, stomach pain, constipation, and dry mouth. If these symptoms are severe or persistent, inform your doctor. Serious side effects, though rare, include hives, skin rash, itching, difficulty breathing or swallowing, swelling of the face, throat, tongue, lips, eyes, hands, feet, ankles, or lower legs, and hoarseness. If you experience any of these, contact your doctor immediately. Some patients taking similar medications for extended periods have developed a condition where the stomach muscles weaken and shrink, though it is unclear if esomeprazole increases this risk. Animal studies have shown that esomeprazole may cause stomach tumors, but it is unknown if this applies to humans. Discuss the risks of taking esomeprazole with your doctor. If you experience any unusual problems, report them to your doctor. Serious side effects can also be reported to the FDA’s MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program. Store esomeprazole in its original container, tightly closed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excessive heat and moisture (not in the bathroom). Dispose of expired or unneeded medication properly, and consult your pharmacist for guidance on disposal. In case of overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual collapses or is not breathing, call 911. Symptoms of overdose may include confusion, drowsiness, blurred vision, rapid heartbeat, upset stomach, sweating, flushing, headache, and dry mouth. Keep all appointments with your doctor. Do not share your medication with others. Consult your pharmacist if you have questions about refilling your prescription.
